name: Olson Sheet Metal Works Inc
old_description: Olson’s Sheet Metal Works is Family owned and operated, Established in 1928 by my grandfather, Clifford E. Olson, operated by his son Robert C Olson, and now run by Robert Dale Olson for a third generation, based in Minneapolis Minnesota.
about:
Olson Sheet Metal Works Inc has operated in Minneapolis, Minnesota since 1928, when Clifford E. Olson founded the business. The company remains family-owned and is now led by the third generation, Robert Dale Olson, following his father Robert C. Olson.

The shop provides complete layout and fabrication of custom metalwork, handling shearing (up to 10-foot capacity), bending with hand brakes and a 10-foot 300-ton press brake, sheet rolling, tube and angle rolling, and a range of welding processes including spot, stick, MIG, and TIG. Plasma and torch cutting, as well as polishing, round out the in-house capabilities. The firm works with a broad palette of metals — stainless steel, carbon steel, galvanized, hot- and cold-rolled, copper, aluminum, brass, bronze, zinc, and even precious metals such as gold and silver — in forms from flat sheet and plate to structural shapes and tubing.

Projects span architectural metalwork such as railings, staircases, hoods, copper roofs, and planter boxes, as well as custom furniture, display fixtures, sinks, counters, and hardware. The customer base includes architects, contractors, designers, and homeowners seeking one-off or small-run pieces for residential and commercial spaces.

The company emphasizes its ability to produce virtually any metal component under one roof, a capability rooted in its third-generation family ownership and full in-house fabrication.

name: Olsun Electrics Corporation
old_description: Nothing less than what you’d expect from Olsun Electrics since 1950
about:
Olsun Electrics Corporation operates from Richmond, Illinois, where it was established in 1950 to serve the electronics industry in the greater Chicago area. The company began in a downtown Richmond building that housed a dentist office in front and a hand-crafted dry-type transformer operation in the back. Gus Asta, one of the original partners, purchased the business in 1965 and expanded the product scope to power and distribution transformers and reactors. The company remains family-run and, on October 28, 2019, earned Women's Business Enterprise (WBE) certification through WBENC, confirming it is at least 51% owned, operated, and controlled by women.

The company designs and manufactures dry-type transformers ranging from 5 kVA through 5,000 kVA in voltage classes up to 34.5 kV, offering 15 distinct product types that include general-purpose, substation, encapsulated, cast-coil, pad-mounted, marine-duty, harmonic-mitigating, and triplex designs. In-house capabilities span design engineering, coil winding (barrel, disc, and block), vacuum-pressure impregnation, core cutting and stacking, enclosure fabrication — now aided by a Bystronic 4 kW fiber laser with automated material handling — powder coating, encapsulation, bus-bar fabrication, and final assembly and testing to NEMA ST-20 and ANSI C57.12.01/91 standards.

Olsun serves a broad range of sectors: universities and student housing, hospitals and healthcare, oil and gas (including portable power for land rigs), petrochemical plants, renewable natural gas and battery energy storage, electric-vehicle charging infrastructure, commercial HVAC OEMs, architectural glass fabrication, ship-to-shore crane systems, and marine/offshore installations (ABS/DNV compliant). The company also supports brand-label and OEM accounts, a segment it has served continuously since the 1960s.

Olsun emphasizes design flexibility and craftsmanship as its differentiators: the ability to produce one-of-a-kind custom transformers when off-the-shelf units will not fit, backed by decades-experienced coil winders and engineers. The firm was founded to meet exacting OEM requirements and continues to position itself as a partner for intricate, standards-compliant solutions rather than a commodity supplier.

The company manufactures a range of electrical components including current and potential transformers, switchgear components, custom transformers, T-Bar switches, fuel pumps, relays, and custom-wound coils.

Its customer base spans aerospace and avionics, military and defense, commercial power distribution, data centers, and solar farms. Named clients include BAE Systems, Eaton, General Dynamics, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon Technologies, Siemens, the U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, and the Department of Defense.

The company cites its ISO 9001 certification and a family-employee-client ethos as the foundation of its integrity.

name: Omni Defense Tech
old_description: Our goal is to enable and enhance mission readiness by offering safe and reliable in-flight relief options for aviators. Omni Defense Technologies designs, develops, and manufactures best-in-class products that support military Aviators on all aircrew ensembles.  Skydrate's Certified Through-Suit Connector maintains environmental seal for Immersion Suits and CBRN Personal Protection Gear, bringing a higher level of performance to the flight deck.
about:
Omni Defense Tech was founded on November 20, 1998 in Colchester, Vermont by Mark Harvie, an electromechanical engineer with a passion for aviation and technology. The company began as a small engineering firm focused on solving life-support challenges for aviators.

Today the company designs, develops, and manufactures in-flight bladder relief systems under the SKYDRATE brand, along with certified through-suit connectors that maintain environmental seals for immersion suits and chemical-biological-radiological-nuclear (CBRN) protective gear. Its product line includes male and female relief devices and tactical flotation systems for parachutists. Omni Defense holds eleven U.S. patents and collaborates with NASA on waste-management systems for astronauts, with products deployed worldwide.

The primary customers are military aviators, including U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy pilots and partner-nation forces, as well as chem-bio protection personnel, search-and-rescue teams, and medical professionals. The SKYDRATE system has passed rigorous flight-safety testing by the USAF and USN and is used on platforms such as the F-15E. NASA also relies on the company's technology for spaceflight waste management.

The business was started to address tactical dehydration, which can reduce pilot performance by 57 percent, and to provide a relief method that does not require aircrew to unstrap from safety restraints. The company emphasizes that its connectors are certified to maintain suit integrity in extreme environments, and that its hands-free, leak-proof design sets a new standard for in-flight bladder relief.

name: Ontogen Medtech
old_description: No hand-waving, just hands-on. The one-stop medtech partner built on strategy and efficiency.
about:
Ontogen Medtech operates from Lisle, Illinois, and began in 2021 with a mission to give medical device innovators a strategy-focused, capital-efficient path from concept to commercialization. The company does not disclose its ownership structure or founders by name.

The firm provides end-to-end product development, including design, prototyping, engineering, and comprehensive in-house testing and validation, alongside ISO 13485 certified contract manufacturing and regulatory support. Its team integrates senior talent directly into client programs to execute prototyping, engineering, and testing rather than only advising. The company reports that its clients have collectively secured more than $16.6 million in grant funding, obtained over 132 patents, won $2.2 million in pitch competitions, and shipped thousands of devices nationwide.

Ontogen serves medical device startups and innovators developing electro-mechanical, reusable, surgical, single-use, and diagnostic devices. Named clients include Flow Medical, Stiehl Tech, Innoblative, and Hubly Surgical, which have relied on the company for everything from SBIR grant support and verification testing to 510(k) clearance and commercial launch.

The company says its differentiation lies in acting as a single, end-to-end partner that eliminates handoff gaps, embedding senior staff in the trenches to deliver tangible deliverables—clear requirements, disciplined design history files, risk rigor, and verification plans—rather than racking up meetings. It describes itself as the most transparent partner in medtech, focusing on evidence over activity.

We offer laser cutting, welding, and installation services to provide a one-stop solution for all your HVAC needs, whether for new construction or property rehabilitation projects.
about:
P&S International Supply Corp operates from Miami, Florida, where it manufactures custom HVAC ductwork and sheet metal components. The company runs a fabrication facility at 3740 NW 78th Street equipped with multiple in-house laser machines, serving both local and international markets.

The shop produces round, spiral, rectangular, and oval ductwork along with custom elbows, offsets, transitions, roof curbs, and adapters. Primary material is galvanized steel, with stainless steel, aluminum, and black iron also available. Processes include laser cutting, welding, and full sheet metal fabrication. The company also provides takeoffs, duct lists, and quotes from project plans, and can supply sheet metal coils, mechanical equipment, air conditioners, and spare parts. Installation services are offered primarily in Florida, with out-of-state projects considered by scope.

P&S serves mechanical contractors, general contractors, and developers in HVAC, commercial construction, new construction, and property rehabilitation. A noted project is the 250,000-square-foot Elev8 Fun facility in Jensen Beach, where the company delivered the full mechanical scope including equipment.

The company positions itself as a single-source partner—manufacturer, fabricator, and mechanical supplier—emphasizing fast turnaround and same-day availability for certain orders. Nationwide delivery and worldwide export, with frequent shipments to the Caribbean, Virgin Islands, and Latin America, extend its reach beyond South Florida.

name: PDI Duct
old_description: Custom fabricated PVC and CPVC ductwork, pipe fittings, and industrial ventilation systems designed for corrosive environments.
about:
PDI Duct operates from North Chelmsford, Massachusetts, where it has fabricated PVC and CPVC duct systems since 1976. The business began as Plastic Design Inc. and later became a division of Plastic Design Industries, a company that also encompasses Chemical Systems Services, Inc. No founders are named in the source material.

The company produces custom PVC and CPVC ductwork, pipe fittings, and complete industrial ventilation systems for corrosive environments. Its 30,000-square-foot facility includes a 21,000-square-foot manufacturing floor equipped with nitrogen-purged hot-gas welding stations, two CNC machining centers, a 400-watt CO2 laser, pipe fusion equipment, and deionized-water testing systems. Capabilities span triple-pass hot-gas and extrusion welding, precision machining of flanges and ports, custom assembly of duct runs and manifolds, and engineering support from consultation through delivery. The shop handles orders ranging from single prototypes to full production runs, with standard duct diameters from 6 to 24 inches and larger.

PDI Duct serves chemical processing plants, wastewater treatment facilities, semiconductor manufacturers, pharmaceutical operations, testing laboratories, and general industrial ventilation projects. Its customers include engineers, contractors, and facility teams who specify corrosion-resistant thermoplastic systems for fume exhaust, process ventilation, and air handling.

It also maintains confined-space entry certification for on-site work. All fabrication occurs under one roof in Massachusetts, which the company says keeps quality and lead times under its control.

old_description: Nestled in the rural and wooded landscapes of Wisconsin, PEC Solar provides custom PV Solar design and installation to residential homes. We’re here to help you lower the energy costs to power your home and help the environment at the same time. Why pay for power from the utility company when you can make it yourself?
about:
PEC Solar Company is a locally owned solar installation firm based near Rio, Wisconsin, in the state's rural, wooded region. The business was established by a professional engineer who holds licenses in 11 states and brings more than 14 years of electrical engineering experience, including solar design. It serves residential customers across Madison, Milwaukee, and all of southern Wisconsin.

The company provides turnkey photovoltaic design and installation for homes, handling permitting, shading analysis, and interconnection. Services include roof- and ground-mounted arrays, drone-based 3D site mapping, system monitoring, electric-vehicle charger installation, battery storage, and backup generator (natural gas or propane) installation. It also offers repair and troubleshooting for existing solar arrays. The firm uses components from vetted manufacturers and performs all electrical work to code.

PEC Solar works exclusively with residential homeowners. Its projects range from single-family rooftop systems to ground-mounted arrays on rural properties throughout southern Wisconsin.

The company emphasizes its engineering credentials: it is the only NABCEP-certified PV Design Specialist in Wisconsin, a REC Certified Solar Professional, and holds a master electrician license. It promotes a no-pressure sales approach, promising to advise against solar if it won’t save the customer money.

about:
PM Assembly LLC began in 2002 as a sole proprietorship in Dallas, Texas, equipped with a single printer, pick-and-place machine, reflow oven, and a few hand-solder stations. The company later relocated to a 6,000-square-foot environmentally friendly facility in Farmersville, Texas, and operates as a private limited liability company.

The shop runs two full surface-mount technology lines with five pick-and-place machines capable of 53,000 components per hour, supplemented by wave soldering, selective soldering, cut-and-clinch, automated optical inspection, X-ray inspection, in-circuit testing, BGA rework, hand assembly, and mechanical assembly. It handles both prototype and ongoing production volumes.

PM Assembly serves customers across the Dallas–Fort Worth metro area and nationwide, targeting engineers at large companies and independent entrepreneurs who need printed circuit board assembly and electronic manufacturing services.

The company emphasizes customer service over rapid growth, positioning itself as the “engineer’s friend” and relying on IPC-certified inspectors using AOI, X-ray, and microscopy to meet quality standards, while also offering in-circuit and functional testing per customer procedures.

name: Pacific Transformer
old_description: Custom, distribution, padmount, and PDU transformers (CA plant is secondary to overseas)
about:
Pacific Transformer was founded in 1981 in a garage in Anaheim, California, by three softball teammates who each borrowed $1,300 from their parents. The company remains founder-owned and headquartered in Anaheim, with a domestic production facility that serves as a backup for its international operations in Mexico, Thailand, and China.

The company designs and manufactures custom magnetic components — transformers (1 VA to 1,000 kVA), toroidals, inductors, chokes, and power-supply assemblies — for applications ranging from signal-level to utility-scale. Engineering services include free design, computer modeling, and rapid prototyping; quotes are returned within one business day and wound, tested prototypes ship within two business days from the Anaheim floor. Over 45 million transformers have been shipped to date.

Customers span aerospace (Mars rovers, NASA flight hardware), defense (nuclear submarine systems), medical imaging, EV infrastructure (Tesla Superchargers), professional audio (Trainwreck amplifiers), industrial automation, data centers, and renewable energy. The firm works with both startups needing a single prototype and established manufacturers placing hundreds of units annually.

Pacific Transformer emphasizes “everything around the winding”: free engineering, agency-approval expertise (UL, CSA, CE, ETL, TÜV), a domestic failover facility that mitigates supply-chain risk, and pricing leveraged from its overseas plants. The company holds AS9100D, MIL-PRF-27, ISO 9001, and ITAR registrations.

Customers span healthcare facilities requiring sterile packaging, airlines and duty-free retailers using ICAO-compliant STEBs, food processors, e-commerce shippers, and law-enforcement agencies needing evidence-handling bags. The firm positions itself as a single-source supplier for tamper-evident and security packaging across these sectors.

Management emphasizes its status as a leader in tamper-evident packaging, backed by continuous equipment investment and an internal graphics team that shortens lead times on custom work. The ICAO approval for STEB production underscores its ability to meet stringent international standards.

The company was built on a commitment to environmentally friendly manufacturing, using 100% recycled and recyclable HDPE to reduce waste and greenhouse gas emissions. Its mission emphasizes smart, low-waste packaging handles, turnkey automated equipment, superior product quality, customer service, and long-term partnerships. PakTech's recycled content is certified by SCS Global Services, and it has established recycling partnerships with over 500 businesses to keep handles in a circular loop.

name: Paragon Woodworking
old_description: Paragon is a hybrid spatial consulting and custom fabrication studio, quietly serving Northern Utah's most considered residential addresses. We engineer architectural cabinetry from a single shop floor in Pleasant View, for the architects, designers and homeowners who notice every reveal.
about:
The studio was founded in 2015 by Jon Anglesey, who brought 35 years of hands-on experience designing, building, and installing custom cabinetry. Anglesey established the company to elevate custom cabinetry from a standard trade into an architectural discipline, applying field-tested knowledge to every design and layout that leaves the studio.

The shop produces architectural-grade custom cabinetry and bespoke millwork, specializing in high-precision frameless construction with interlocking blind-dado joinery glued and screwed at every joint. Cabinet boxes use CARB-compliant, formaldehyde-free thermally fused laminate platforms; drawers feature 3/4-inch sidewalls, 1/2-inch bottoms, and Italian Salice rack-and-pinion full-extension slides rated 33 to 50 pounds above competing hardware. Finishes are Italian waterborne urethanes with a proprietary cross-linker, delivering zero-VOC, zero-HAPP surface protection. Two product lines serve different project scopes: the Custom Shop Series offers unrestricted design, shadow-line detailing, and integrated LED case lighting, while the ECO Line standardizes flat-slab profiles with pre-engineered subcrowns to cut field installation time by two-thirds and reduce cost by 25 to 35 percent.

Paragon serves architects, designers, builders, and homeowners across nine Northern Utah counties — Box Elder, Cache, Weber, Davis, Morgan, Salt Lake, Summit, Utah, and Wasatch — covering the entire Wasatch Front corridor. Projects span luxury kitchens, bathroom vanities, integrated library and office systems, entertainment hubs, laundry rooms, and tailored closets. The team manages each commission from initial architectural layout through zero-tolerance final installation.

The company's stated differentiation rests on four pillars: total transparency in materials, pricing, and methods; technical innovation through advanced design software and disciplined fabrication; environmental stewardship via sustainably sourced, low-emission materials; and architectural respect for the client's space, investment, and the timber resources used. Anglesey's direct involvement in every design ensures that details derived from decades of field installation — reveal alignment, drawer load capacity, joinery that accommodates structural settlement — are baked into the plans before fabrication begins.

name: Parts Unlimited Interiors, Inc.
old_description: Parts Unlimited Interiors is one of those successful entrepreneurial business stories where one thing has led to another, and the small company continues to expand and grow in a controlled, logical fashion. Literally founded physically in a 1964 Corvair's trunk (so to speak), PUI has expanded to the Morrises' basement, to the Jefferson Trade Center in December of 1984, to a 51,400-square foot facility in Louisville, KY, and currently to a 120,000-square foot facility in Oldham County Business Park, La Grange, KY that houses over 100 employees. Approximately 97% to 98% of Parts Unlimited Interiors products are manufactured in the USA, while eight to nine percent of product sales are attributed to being items manufactured overseas. Having most of the parts produced in the United States and most of the sales attributed to U.S. made parts is a success story in and of itself. But Parts Unlimited Interiors isn't resting on its laurels.
about:
Parts Unlimited Interiors, Inc. is based in La Grange, Kentucky, operating from a 120,000-square-foot facility in the Oldham County Business Park. The business traces its origins to 1974 when Rollo Fox and his wife Colleen, inspired by Colleen's father H.V. Morris, attended a Corvair convention in Chicago and sold parts from their car trunk. What began as a new-old-stock parts venture soon evolved into manufacturing Corvair interior components, then expanded to other GM models. The company moved from the Morris family basement to the Jefferson Trade Center in December 1984, then to a 51,400-square-foot plant in Louisville, before settling in its current location. Since October 2023, PUI has been a subsidiary of Classic Industries, following an earlier acquisition by Restoration Parts Unlimited in 2013.

PUI manufactures interior soft-trim and hard-goods for classic American vehicles, including seat upholstery, door panels, headliners, window felts, and insulation products. Production relies on a mix of computer-controlled machinery and hands-on oversight by more than 80 artisans, many with decades of tenure. The facility houses sophisticated equipment for cutting, sewing, and assembling a wide range of materials. Approximately 97–98% of PUI's products are made in the United States, with the remainder sourced overseas. The company maintains a large inventory to support same-day and next-day shipping on stocked items.

The company serves the automotive aftermarket and classic-car restoration markets, supplying wholesale dealers and individual restorers. Its product lines cover GM brands (Chevrolet Impala, Pontiac, Buick), Ford, and Mopar vehicles. PUI sells through over 100 dealers across the U.S. and internationally, and offers exclusive wholesale pricing to registered partners.

The Foxes originally started the business to address the finite supply of NOS Corvair parts, shifting to reproduction to keep the company viable. Today, PUI emphasizes domestic manufacturing, a deep catalog of pattern-specific parts, and reduced lead times—raw-material sourcing now takes two to three weeks, and dealer delivery is under one month—following supply-chain improvements after the Classic Industries acquisition.

The company traces its current expansion to 2016, when it began scaling from 30 employees to over 900 and acquired nine companies to build an international portfolio. Chief Executive Mark Dohnalek leads the organization, which operates offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The firm provides collaborative product design, development, engineering, and manufacturing services. Its multidisciplinary teams handle industrial design, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, embedded software development, optical design, prototyping, design for manufacturing (DFM), regulatory support, and global supply chain management. Pivot reports more than 100 engineers, over 300,000 square feet of scalable manufacturing space, FDA‑registered facilities, and production sites in the United States, Mexico, Europe, China, and the Philippines.

Pivot serves clients in medical devices, industrial products, agriculture, sports and entertainment, IoT, embedded electronics, motor control, biometrics and security, touch‑screen technology, optical systems, and the emerging drone (UAV) sector. Its customer base ranges from startups to established manufacturers and global organizations seeking end‑to‑end product lifecycle support.

The company positions itself as a single‑source partner that integrates engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain under one organization to reduce communication gaps and delays. It emphasizes company‑owned global operations, experience in highly regulated industries, flexible engagement models, and a legacy of more than 50 years in product development and manufacturing.

old_description: Great beer isn’t just something you drink — it’s something you share. We’re obsessed with quality and driven by experimentation, chasing flavors worth talking about, and creating a place you’ll want to come back to.
about:
Pivotal Brewing Company operates from a historic mill building in Bristol, Rhode Island. The brewery and taproom opened with a focus on quality and experimentation, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company brews a diverse lineup of craft beers ranging from crisp modern lagers and hop-forward hazy IPAs to seasonal releases and small-batch experiments. Production takes place on-site, feeding a taproom that runs Wednesday through Sunday and a 4,000-square-foot event space with 35- to 45-foot ceilings and large windows. The venue accommodates semi-private gatherings of 20 to 120 guests and full buyouts for up to 450 people.

The taproom serves walk-in customers seeking craft beer, live music, trivia nights, and family-friendly events such as storytime sessions. The event side hosts weddings, corporate functions, birthday parties, and welcome receptions. The company also distributes its beer through the taproom and likely through local accounts, though specific distribution channels are not detailed.

Founders describe the mission as being "obsessed with quality and driven by experimentation, chasing flavors worth talking about, and creating a place you'll want to come back to." The historic mill setting and dog-friendly policy are highlighted as part of the experience.

old_description: Planet Plastics is a leading manufacturer of lighting components for the commercial, architectural, hospitality, OEM and custom lighting industries. We manufacture plastic light diffusers and replacement lenses for fluorescent, LED and HID lighting fixtures.
about:
Planet Plastics Co has operated from Chino, California for over 50 years. The company describes itself as a global plastic molding company, though no founding year or founder names are disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

The company manufactures plastic lighting components — diffusers and replacement lenses for fluorescent, LED, and HID fixtures — as well as point-of-purchase retail displays, motion-picture and theme-park props, food-case displays, museum displays, spheres, hemispheres, and other custom fabricated products. Its 43,000-square-foot facility houses a complete plastics fabrication operation: 3-axis and 5-axis CNC routing and cutting, vacuum forming, drape forming, free-form blow molding, thermoforming, laser cutting and etching, die cutting, printing, acrylic fabrication, drilling, sanding, sand blasting, gluing and bonding, flame polishing, buff polishing, line bending, and custom packaging fulfillment. The company says it ships any quantity from one piece to millions.

Customers span commercial, architectural, hospitality, OEM, and custom lighting markets; specialty retailers, restaurants, and brand merchandisers for POP displays; motion-picture and theme-park production; food-service equipment; and museum exhibits. The staff works with designers and engineers to develop parts from concept through production.

Planet Plastics emphasizes customer service, customization, and a satisfaction pledge: every order is treated as the most important, with no minimum quantity, custom kitting, and a commitment to resolve any quality issue. The company cites its uniquely large oven capacity and press forming capability as enabling projects that might otherwise seem impossible.

name: Plastech Inc
old_description: Plastech Inc. is a Custom Plastic Injection Molding company that works with a broad range of diverse customers in various industries throughout the United States. We focus on quality injection molding, tool and die, prototypes, assembly, and secondary manufacturing operations.
about:
Plastech Inc. operates from Corvallis, Oregon, where it has been based since 1976. The business traces its roots to 1970, when Al Hendrickson founded an injection molding operation in Rancho Cordova, California. After relocating to the Corvallis Airport Industrial Park, the company was renamed Hendrickson Enterprises. In 1996, Al’s son Michael Hendrickson purchased the business, incorporated it, and changed the name to Plastech Inc. The firm remains family-owned and is currently led by Michael Hendrickson, with his daughter and son-in-law serving as key employees.

The company provides custom plastic injection molding along with a full suite of turnkey services: tool and die making (both domestic and offshore), CNC machining, rapid prototyping including 3D printing and fabrication, secondary operations, electro-mechanical assembly, and packaging. Production runs on seven injection molding machines ranging from 85 to 400 tons within a 12,500-square-foot manufacturing facility supported by 6,700 square feet of warehouse space. Plastech employs 14 family members, though total headcount is not disclosed.

Plastech serves a diverse customer base across industries including electronics, dental, sporting goods, pool and spa, consumer products, trucking, industrial, education, medical, and aerospace. The company works with clients both domestically and internationally, managing tooling partnerships with three offshore factories that have been in place for over 20 years.

Plastech emphasizes a customer-focused partnership model, aiming to be more than a manufacturer by offering design-for-manufacturing support and long-term service relationships. The company’s mission centers on delivering quality products at competitive prices through collaborative team environments.

name: PlastiCert
old_description: PlastiCert can provide you composite injection molding expertise in an environment that fosters personal growth, professional challenge and a recognized responsibility to the community.
about:
PlastiCert was established in 1981 in Lewiston, Minnesota. The company has over four decades of experience in injection molding.

The company specializes in complex injection molding for engineered thermoplastics, including standard resins such as polycarbonate, ABS, and nylon, as well as high-temperature materials like Ultem, Ryton, and PEEK. Its vertically integrated operation combines engineering support (DFM, mold-flow analysis, material guidance), an in-house tool shop for mold design, construction, repair, and maintenance, and production capabilities that encompass insert molding, overmolding, long-fiber reinforced resins, and mold-transfer recovery programs. Recurring production volumes typically range from 2,000 to 5,000 parts per month, adjusted for part size and complexity, with additional capacity for prototyping and short runs.

PlastiCert serves OEMs in industrial, aerospace, medical, agricultural, electronics, and telecommunications sectors. Notable customer examples include a telecommunications antenna manufacturer and a medical device manufacturer, as well as commercial and consumer recreational product companies.

The firm differentiates itself by keeping engineering, tooling, and molding under one roof to avoid handoff gaps, and by focusing on technically demanding programs rather than commodity pricing. It has earned four Top Shop awards from Plastics Technology magazine.

old_description: Delivering ROI Focused Master-Class Electronics, Quality Components and Collaborative Engineering Design to the Global Market Since 1973.
about:
Founded in 1973 in Elkhart, Indiana, Poly Electronics has operated as a privately held electronics manufacturer for over five decades. The company began as a provider of printed circuit board assembly and has since expanded into a full-service partner for design, engineering, supply chain management, and distribution.

Today, Poly Electronics delivers integrated PCB solutions encompassing surface-mount (SMT), through-hole (THT), and hybrid assembly, along with box build, potting, and testing services that include flying probe and 3D automated optical inspection. The firm offers design-for-manufacturability consulting, component sourcing through a vetted global network, and warehousing with global distribution. Over its history, the company has engineered more than 3,500 custom electrical products.

Poly Electronics serves customers in sectors such as aviation, automotive, and industrial equipment, citing long-term relationships with companies including Vanair, Cargo Van & More, and Montego Dev. Many clients have remained with the company for 20 years or more, relying on its ability to manage component obsolescence and raw-material price fluctuations.

The company emphasizes a collaborative model, positioning itself as an extension of the customer’s team with quote turnaround of 48–72 hours for production-ready projects and solution delivery in as little as four weeks. Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015, and it reports a 99.97% functionality rate on delivered items. Investment in equipment such as KOHYOUNG 3D AOI and flying probe testers supports its focus on consistent, on-time delivery.

name: Poly Plastics Inc.
old_description: Poly Plastics, Inc. Has been family owned and operated since 1992.
about:
Poly Plastics Inc. is a family-owned flexible packaging manufacturer based in Ferris, Texas. The company was founded in 1992 and has remained under family operation since its inception. With over four decades of experience in the packaging sector, the business began by serving flexible packaging needs with a focus on personal service.

The company produces custom printed and plain plastic bags, roll stock, pouches, and laminated films. Its production capabilities include flexographic, rotogravure, and digital printing, supported by in-house prepress, laser etching, and plate making. Additional services encompass rewinding, slitting, film lamination, bag making, and digital label printing. All products are manufactured using FDA-approved films such as polyethylene, polypropylene, cast-polypropylene, acrylic, and polyester.

Poly Plastics serves a broad range of food and industrial markets. Its customer base includes manufacturers of baked goods, fresh-cut produce, health and personal care items, nuts and dried fruit, snacks, tortilla chips, spices, pet food, confectionery, frozen foods, ice, industrial products, popsicles, dried grains, tortillas, and fortune cookies. The company also provides branding and design services to help food and beverage manufacturers activate strategic programs and improve shelf life.

The company emphasizes customer satisfaction as its primary goal, offering personal service and full-service delivery to the customer's door. Its FDA-approved films and in-house prepress capabilities are cited as key differentiators that enable quick turnaround and quality control for food packaging applications.

name: Port Clinton Manufacturing Co
old_description: More than making individual parts, PCM specializes in mating parts together through various methods including brazing and mechanical fits producing a precision assembly for additional machining or ready for assembly.
about:
Port Clinton Manufacturing Co. has operated from Port Clinton, Ohio, since its founding in 1929. The company remains a closely held family corporation, locally owned and operated across nearly a century of continuous service.

A broaching department runs 12 machines with a 54-inch stroke and 15-ton capacity, while grinding operations cover ID, OD, centerless, double-disk, and Blanchard processes. Secondary machining includes thread rolling, knurling, drilling, tapping, cross drilling, deep-hole drilling, honing, milling, tumbling, bead blasting, and a range of cutoff and forming operations. Heat treating and coating are managed through a qualified external network. The company also performs ultrasonic cleaning and Millipore particle-count testing. Precision assemblies — joined by brazing or mechanical fits — are produced in-house, either as finished units or as in-process components brought to final tolerance after assembly.

Primary markets include railroad, oil and gas, mining, emergency power generation, agricultural and construction equipment, mine safety devices, heavy-truck transmissions, and brake systems. As a tier 1 supplier to major engine manufacturers, the shop supports PPAP requirements and has maintained relationships with several Fortune 500 customers for more than 50 years.

The business emphasizes integrity, fair dealing, and continuous improvement to reduce cost while preserving quality. Its quality program targets zero defects, backed by CMM, optical comparator, surface-finish, Magnaflux, and Rockwell hardness inspection, and has earned a Dun & Bradstreet AAA rating.

name: Port Plastics
old_description: Port Plastics delivers industrial plastic materials and custom fabrication services to manufacturers nationwide through 11 strategically located facilities.
about:
Port Plastics was founded in 1960 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a regional supplier of industrial plastic materials to local manufacturers. Over six decades, the company expanded from a single location to a national network of 11 facilities positioned near major manufacturing hubs, including Houston for energy, San Jose for semiconductor, and Phoenix for aerospace and defense.

The company distributes high-performance engineering plastics — stocking more than 1,000 material grades such as PEEK, PTFE, Vespel, Torlon, and Ultem — and operates in-house fabrication shops equipped with precision CNC machining centers, CNC routers, and panel saws capable of cutting 5-inch-thick sheet up to 11 feet long. Services include routing, drilling, thermoforming, welding, and high-tolerance machining to ±0.001 inch, with same-day cutting and next-day delivery from local inventory.

Port Plastics serves semiconductor manufacturers requiring FM4910-compliant ultra-high-purity materials for wet benches and vacuum chambers; energy and oil-and-gas clients specifying NORSOK M-710-qualified components for subsea wellheads and sour-gas environments; aerospace and defense contractors needing AS9100D-compliant, FAR 25.853-compliant materials for structural panels, seals, and insulation; medical device makers using USP Class VI and ISO 10993 biocompatible polymers; and food processors relying on FDA 21 CFR 177 and NSF-certified materials for conveyor components and tank liners.

The company positions itself as a technical partner rather than a pure material supplier, emphasizing its staff of materials engineers averaging 15-plus years of plastics experience, full traceability documentation on every shipment, and a quality system certified to ISO 9001:2015 with additional AS9100D and ITAR registrations. Deep inventory positions and multiple source relationships are maintained to buffer customers against supply disruptions.

name: Portland Bottling Company
old_description: For the most trusted, safest and highest quality ready-to-drink beverages in the industry, Portland Bottling Company is ready to deliver.
about:
Portland Bottling Company, founded in 1924, operates from Clackamas, Oregon, in the Portland metropolitan area. For nearly a century it has served as a fixture of the Pacific Northwest beverage industry, running multiple production, storage, and repacking facilities totaling roughly 500,000 square feet. The company is privately held; no specific ownership designation such as family- or veteran-owned is stated in public sources.

The company specializes in contract packing of ready-to-drink beverages in aluminum cans. Its capabilities cover filling, cartoning, secondary packaging, and warehousing. The canning line runs at up to 1,450 cans per minute and handles can sizes from 8.4 oz to 16 oz, with options for cold fill, tunnel pasteurization, liquid nitrogen dosing, reverse‑osmosis water treatment, and both liquid and granulated sweeteners. Cartoning equipment produces 4‑, 6‑, 8‑, 10‑, 12‑, and 24‑pack configurations, plus variety packs and registered film shrink wrap. On‑site and off‑site warehousing with 24/7 security supports distribution.

Portland Bottling works with and independent beverage brands across the Pacific Northwest and nationwide, shipping throughout the western United States and Canada. Its customer base includes producers of carbonated juices and waters, energy drinks, functional beverages, organic‑certified drinks, kosher beverages, and gluten‑free products.

The company emphasizes proactive partnership, treating customers’ resources as its own and maintaining rigorous quality systems. It holds FSSC 22000 certification, adheres to HACCP, and carries organic (QAI), gluten‑free (GFCO), and kosher (OU) certifications. Inline monitoring, on‑site QA labs, and third‑party audits underpin its quality assurance, while a “people‑first” culture aims to enable solutions at every production stage.

about:
Portland Garment Factory (PGF) operates in Portland, Oregon. Founded in 2008 by Britt Howard, the studio is a woman-owned business certified by WBENC and a Certified B Corporation. It began as a zero-waste creative design and fabrication studio aiming to upend the traditional factory model through ethical labor practices and environmental sustainability.

PGF provides full-service creative design and fabrication, specializing in custom cut-and-sew manufacturing, art fabrication, product development, prototyping, and retail and experiential fabrication. The studio handles projects ranging from one-off installations to clothing production runs of 20,000-plus units. A team of 11 to 50 employees works in-house on fabrication, design, and experimentation through the PGF Lab, an internal incubator for unconventional projects.

Clients include major brands such as Nike, Adidas, Intel, Xbox, Converse, Tillamook, and agencies like Wieden+Kennedy, as well as artists and institutions including the Portland Art Museum and Portland Japanese Garden. Industries served span apparel manufacturing, retail display and installation, experiential marketing, public art and sculpture, corporate branding and merchandise, museum and cultural exhibits, sports and entertainment, and food and beverage packaging.

The company differentiates itself through a zero-waste philosophy, ethical labor practices, and a commitment to environmental sustainability. Its stated mission is to create work with intention and serve the community, guided by core values of being human, thinking forward, honoring process, respecting time, and inviting challenge.

about:
Power Engineering & Manufacturing, Ltd. (PEM) was founded in 1975 by Saul Herscovici and members of the Warren family in Waterloo, Iowa. The company began as a specialist in custom gearbox design and has since grown into a full-service manufacturer of heavy-duty gearboxes serving customers across the United States and in more than 48 countries.

PEM designs, machines, assembles, and tests custom gearboxes from its Waterloo facility, which houses 12 CNC lathes, five CNC mills, two Okuma MCR-A5CII double-column machining centers, six CNC hobbing machines, five gear grinders, and a range of grinding, shaping, keyseating, welding, and inspection equipment. The shop can handle parts up to 78.7 inches in diameter and 96 inches in length, and offers reverse engineering, rebuild, and reconditioning services for virtually any make of gearbox, including Falk, Demag, Flender, and dozens of other OEM brands. In-house capabilities include finite-element analysis, proprietary gear-design software, magnetic-particle and visual inspection, and two large-capacity CMMs.

The company's gearboxes operate in demanding applications such as U.S. Navy AD-43 systems, helicopter test stands, and roll crushers, and it supports maintenance and upgrade programs for industrial OEMs across sectors including defense, aerospace, mining, and general heavy industry. PEM also provides expedited manufacturing, climate-controlled warehousing, and 24/7 exchange programs for critical spares.

PEM emphasizes exceeding AGMA standards and achieving high power density through its MEGAGEAR® technology, which can increase horsepower or torque by up to 35 percent over original designs. The firm cites ingenuity, relentless attention to detail, and remarkable customer service as its defining differentiators, backed by an ISO 9001:2015 quality system and welding procedures qualified to AWS and NAVSEA standards.

Precise Circuit Company was founded in 1985 by Thomas Misencik in downtown Shelton, Connecticut. The company began as a provider of quality electronic assemblies for small to mid-sized original equipment manufacturers, specializing in surface-mount, through-hole, and mixed-technology printed circuit board assembly. It remains owned and operated by the Misencik family, with Tom Misencik Sr. and Tom Misencik Jr. serving as the primary owners.

The facility also maintains a climate-controlled board storage room and provides consignment or turnkey procurement options.

Precise Circuit serves original equipment manufacturers in the electronics sector, typically small to mid-sized companies that require prototype through production-volume assemblies. The company works directly with OEMs across industrial, commercial, and defense-related electronics, though specific industry verticals are not publicly listed beyond the general OEM market.

The company emphasizes direct owner involvement, long-term customer relationships, and a commitment to quality, transparency, and competitive pricing. Community engagement includes mentoring the Shelton High School FIRST Robotics team.

The company’s flagship product is the Summit™ 4K single-use surgical arthroscope, a sterile, ready-to-use rigid endoscope that eliminates reprocessing, maintenance contracts, and sterilization delays. Pristine pairs the hardware with Pristine Connect®, a cloud-based platform that automates inventory management, stores images and video, and provides digital training checklists. A subscription model, branded Scopes as a Subscription™, replaces capital equipment purchases with predictable per-procedure pricing. The product pipeline extends to laparoscopy and flexible endoscopy, targeting a global addressable market of 125 million procedures annually.

Pristine serves hospital operating rooms, ambulatory surgery centers, and orthopedic practices. Early adopters include Southern California Orthopedic Institute, UCLA, Hospital for Special Surgery, Virtua Health in New Jersey, Doral Surgery Center in Florida, and Stetson Lee Orthopaedics in California. The company’s advisory board comprises surgeons specializing in shoulder, knee, elbow, and sports medicine.

Pristine was started to remove inefficiency, variability, and safety risks from the endoscopy suite. By delivering a new high-definition scope for every case, the company aims to reduce staff exposure to contaminated instruments, accelerate room turnover, and provide transparent, automated economics for surgical visualization.

about:
Pyramid Semiconductor is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California. The company was formed in January 2003 when it acquired the product lines of Performance Semiconductor. In March 2021, HEICO Corporation's Electronic Technologies Group acquired Pyramid Semiconductor, and the business now operates as part of HEICO/3D PLUS USA in Silicon Valley.

Pyramid Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor manufacturer producing integrated circuits including MIL-STD-1750A processors, SRAMs, EEPROMs, FCT/FCT-T logic, and multi-chip modules. Wafers are fabricated at outside foundries (TSMC in Taiwan and LA Semiconductor in the USA), while the company's 10,000-square-foot Sunnyvale facility handles wafer testing, ceramic clean-room assembly, burn-in, environmental testing, electrical testing, marking, and quality assurance. The company supports over 100 Standard Military Drawings (SMDs) and offers custom logic functions and packaging with short lead times.

The company serves military, aerospace, industrial, and commercial markets. Its MIL-STD-1750A processors have been used by military customers for over two decades, and its QML-certified manufacturing line supports more than 100 SMDs for defense and aerospace programs. Industrial and commercial customers use its SRAMs, EEPROMs, and logic devices in embedded systems requiring high reliability and long-term supply.

Pyramid Semiconductor positions itself as a sole-source supplier committed to long-term availability of legacy MIL-STD-1750A products. It emphasizes a secure, independent supply chain with established foundry relationships and in-house assembly and test capabilities to ensure continued availability and short lead times for custom solutions.

Quantum Imaging operates as SCD USA Infrared LLC, a U.S. subsidiary of Israel-based Semiconductor Devices (SCD), from its headquarters in Colorado Springs, Colorado. The company leverages more than four decades of infrared detector development and manufacturing experience accumulated by its parent organization.

The company designs and manufactures infrared detectors and camera cores across the short-wave (SWIR), mid-wave (MWIR), and long-wave (LWIR) spectral bands. Its product lines include the Blackbird, Cardinal, Bird, and Pelican families, offered as integrated detector dewar cooler assemblies (IDDCAs) and complete camera engines. Manufacturing encompasses III-V semiconductor material growth, VLSI read-out integrated circuit design, and environmental qualification testing for harsh defense environments. Tens of thousands of detectors have been produced for deployment.

Primary customers operate in defense, aerospace, security and surveillance, and commercial sectors. Defense programs include airborne, land, naval, and missile applications such as intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), missile warning, and situational awareness. A noted example is a 2020 agreement to supply Raytheon with SWIR cameras and optical sensor packages. Commercial applications span aviation safety, gas sensing, non-destructive testing, semiconductor inspection, and process monitoring. Space imaging is also served.

The company states its mission is to deliver innovative, field-ready, intelligent imaging and detection systems that enable real-time visualization of mission-critical intelligence in all theaters and environments. It differentiates itself through a broad product portfolio, scalable engine and camera architectures, and the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with infrared sensor technology.

about:
Randy's Booth Co. Inc. operates from Crystal, Minnesota, a northwest suburb of Minneapolis. The business traces its roots to the 1970s when Randy Kissoondath, an immigrant from Trinidad and Tobago, began building restaurant booths and established a national reputation through word of mouth. After a hiatus, Randy restarted the company at age 58, and his son Bert Kissoondath, now CEO, took full ownership following his father's sudden death in 2009. The firm has remained family-owned through two generations.

The company manufactures custom hospitality furnishings — booths, chairs, stools, tables, banquettes, and headboards — from Northern Hardwoods including cherry, ash, oak, and maple. A team of 20 craftspeople works in a renovated facility on two acres that the company moved into in September 2017. The building provides 20-foot ceiling clearance, a loading dock, a showroom, and combined office and production space that Bert credits for improved throughput and profitability.

Designers, architects, and builders across the United States specify Randy's Booth for restaurant, lounge, healthcare, corporate office, and residential projects. Long-standing accounts include hotel chains such as Hyatt and Perkins, and local landmarks like Mancini's Char House, Nye's, and O'Gara's. Recent work includes custom booths and furnishings for the Nova Restaurant Group's Hazelwood Food & Drink and multiple concepts for restaurateurs Kam Talebi and Luke Derheim.

Bert Kissoondath says the company was built on his father's insistence that everything be handmade and that pride in workmanship shows in the finished product. That philosophy earned the firm the 2024 Minnesota Manufacturer of the Year award and the SBA's Minnesota Family Owned Business of the Year honor. Clients cite the team's integrity, on-time delivery, budget adherence, and willingness to value-engineer as reasons they return.

The company emphasizes a Shingo Model‑grounded Enterprise Excellence framework and a set of cultural values — champion innovation, deliver quality, be customer‑ and patient‑centric, drive urgency, act with integrity, embrace continuous improvement, and grow together. name: Revolution Bag
old_description: Delta Plastics of the South is founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas, with a focus on providing efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South, and soon after starts recycling to show the importance of being part of the solution to plastic waste.
about:
Revolution Bag operates from Little Rock, Arkansas, tracing its roots to 1996 when Delta Plastics of the South was founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas. The family-owned company began by providing efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South and quickly added recycling operations to address plastic waste.

Today the company runs an integrated circular platform that collects, cleans, and mechanically recycles more than 300 million pounds of flexible film each year, producing certified post-consumer and post-industrial resins. Those resins feed its own manufacturing lines, which turn out trash-can liners under the Revolution Bag brand, carryout bags for foodservice, grocery, and retail, high-performance agricultural films, commercial sheeting, and stretch films. The business has grown through acquisitions including Rodeo Plastic Bag & Film, Command Packaging, Encore Recycling, Pak-Sher, Polar Plastics, Jadcore, and Five Point Films.

Customers span agriculture, food service, grocery, retail, construction, and waste management, as well as global brands and OEMs that incorporate Revolution’s recycled resins into their own products. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, for example, reports cutting virgin resin use from hundreds of thousands of pounds to 17,000 pounds annually through the partnership.

The company says it was started to show the importance of being part of the solution to plastic waste, and it now champions a “sustainable loop” model that controls the entire lifecycle of plastics to create value for customers and reduce environmental impact.

about:
Rockett Inc. was founded in 1906 in Flowood, Mississippi, beginning as a small machine shop serving local industrial needs. The company has remained a private, Mississippi-based operation for over a century, evolving from its early roots into a comprehensive contract manufacturer.

Today, Rockett operates a 200,000-square-foot facility with more than 80 employees and over 50 pieces of fabrication equipment. Its capabilities span custom metal fabrication, CNC machining (including 3- and 4-axis milling, turning, turret punching, laser and plasma cutting), forming, and welding (MIG, TIG, submerged arc, high-frequency pulse) with AWS D1.1-certified welders. The shop also runs two powder-coating lines and produces forged steel wheels, NEMA-rated electrical enclosures, oil-tight transformer tanks, and tunnel kiln cars. Materials processed include mild and stainless steel, aluminum, copper, brass, and specialty alloys.

Rockett serves industries such as electric energy, power transmission and distribution, motor generation, material handling, brick and ceramics, furnaces and kilns, and steelmaking, shipping finished goods and subassemblies across the United States and overseas. Customers range from OEMs requiring limited-run production to partners needing just-in-time delivery schedules.

The company emphasizes a “From Print to Paint” approach, integrating 3D CAD design, precision fabrication, welding, finishing, and quality control under one roof. Its stated mission is to deliver competitively priced, on-time manufactured goods through continuous improvement, while valuing quality, safety, and integrity as highly as productivity.

The pair produced components for the U.S. Army during World War II, and by the 1950s they had built their first injection molding machine from scratch, laying the groundwork for a plastics-focused operation. The shop provides injection molding, product assembly, Bridgeport milling, custom fabrication, quality control, and 3D printing services. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and is UL-approved, with calibration and documentation traceable to NIST standards. Rockford Molded Products emphasizes quality as its defining differentiator, citing over 80 years of continuous operation, ISO 9001:2015 certification, UL approval, and a QMS traceable to NIST standards as evidence of its commitment to delivering 100 percent good parts.

The firm provides a range of engineering and manufacturing services centered on wire harnesses, electronic controls, and prototype development. Its capabilities span controls engineering, electronics engineering (including digital, analog, and power design), harness engineering (design, routing, packaging, testing, and delivery), and prototype engineering (concept validation, design reviews, test plans, and on‑site support). Rowe also produces RF systems, wireless throttle controls, and custom manufactured assemblies for mobile equipment and other sectors.

Rowe serves customers in agriculture, transportation, recreation, and industrial markets, with a primary focus on mobile equipment manufacturers. The company works with OEMs on projects ranging from accessory integration to complete machine solutions, and collaborates with client engineering teams on both turnkey and subset developments.

Rowe emphasizes a client‑first process that begins with understanding requirements and scales from small pilot projects to larger engagements. It differentiates itself through deep technical experience across the full electrical architecture, the ability to work within a client’s existing software and supply chain, and a prototyping approach that includes periodic design reviews and on‑site data collection.

about:
Roy's Wood Products operates from Lugoff, South Carolina, where Roy Brazell Sr. founded the business in 1962 as a garage shop producing cabinet doors. The company remains family-owned, passing to his son Roy Brazell Jr. in 1985, who expanded the operation to 15,000 square feet. In 2000 the name changed to Roy's Wood Products, Inc., and in 2008 grandsons Jody and Russell Brazell acquired the business, continuing three generations of family leadership.

The firm manufactures a full line of wood components including custom cabinet doors, drawer fronts, dovetail drawer boxes, face frames, hardwood plywood, mouldings, dimensional lumber, and shutters, alongside a range of hardware and accessories. Production takes place in a facility exceeding 61,000 square feet that houses a rough mill and a dedicated cabinet door manufacturing plant, supported by experienced craftsmen and modern equipment.

Its customers span cabinet shops, millwork operations, and building professionals who source both stock and custom wood products for residential and commercial projects. The company supplies both standard and made-to-order items to meet varied project requirements.

The company emphasizes an old-fashioned focus on excellence at a reasonable price, a principle carried through three generations of the Brazell family and reflected in its commitment to quality products and dependable service.

name: Ruben Custom Sawmill and Woodworks, LLC
old_description: Founded by Matt Ruben in 2018, Ruben Custom Sawmill began with a single sawmill and a bold vision: reclaim Minnesota's fallen trees and turn them into lasting works of art. What started as a weekend passion is now a full-time, family-run business trusted by clients across the Twin Cities.
about:
Ruben Custom Sawmill and Woodworks, LLC operates from White Bear Township, Minnesota, in the Twin Cities metro area. The company was founded in 2018 by Matt Ruben, who began with a single portable sawmill and a vision to reclaim fallen Minnesota trees and transform them into lasting works of art. What started as a weekend passion has grown into a full-time, family-run business serving clients across the region.

The shop produces custom furniture including live-edge tables, bar tops, and mantles, as well as butcher-block-style walnut countertops. In addition to finished pieces, Ruben Custom Sawmill offers portable on-site milling services, bringing a Wood-Mizer sawmill directly to a client's property to process logs into kiln-dried slabs and native hardwood lumber available by appointment. The company reports having salvaged over 1,000 trees and completed projects for more than 1,000 clients.

Customers are primarily residential homeowners and DIY enthusiasts in the Twin Cities area who seek one-of-a-kind furniture or need logs milled from their own land. Testimonials reference projects such as a custom black walnut mantel fitted over an existing stone surround, a dining table built from a client's own cherry and burr oak logs, and a coffee table crafted from supplied slabs. The business also works with contractors and designers on custom countertop installations.

Ruben emphasizes care, craftsmanship, and character in every job, whether milling on a client's property or building a dining table in the shop. The founder's original mission — giving fallen trees a second life — remains the guiding principle, and the portable milling capability allows customers to preserve trees that hold personal significance.

about:
S&F Foods, Inc. is a frozen food manufacturer headquartered in Romulus, Michigan, founded in 2003. The company specializes in producing enrobed and topped items for institutional school foodservice programs and retail markets nationwide.

Product offerings include the Original Pull-A-Part Topped Breadsticks and Dave’s Detroit Style Pizza, and the firm processes USDA commodities such as cheese, tomato paste, and flour.

S&F Foods serves institutional school foodservice programs, including the National School Lunch Program, and retail channels nationwide. Its products are distributed to schools and retail outlets across the country.

The company emphasizes food safety and quality, holding BRCGS AA Grade certification, USDA compliance, gluten-free certification from GFCO, and organic certification from Global Organic Alliance. Its mission highlights decades of experience producing safe, certified, and authentic products with ongoing reviews of food safety policies.

old_description: S&W Wholesale was founded in 1978 by Frank & Rosemary Spalitta, lifelong residents of Hammond, Louisiana. They began with a passion for serving local foodservice operators throughout Tangipahoa Parish. Today their son, Paul, continues to grow and build on their legacy by servicing throughout all of Southeast Louisiana and the Mississippi Gulfcoast.
about:
S&W Foods operates from Hammond, Louisiana, where it was founded in 1978 by Frank and Rosemary Spalitta. The family-owned business began by serving foodservice operators throughout Tangipahoa Parish and has since expanded across Southeast Louisiana and the Mississippi Gulf Coast under the leadership of their son, Paul Spalitta, who now serves as president and owner.

The company functions as a broadline distributor, offering a vast selection of food and non‑food items that includes produce, meats, breads, condiments, equipment, smallwares, paper goods, and cleaning supplies. Its distribution facility sits near the I‑55/I‑12 corridor, enabling rapid delivery — notably remaining operational the day after Hurricanes Ida and Katrina. S&W also develops private‑label brands such as Copper Creek Cattle Company and Captain Frank’s Seafood, and runs special programs for custom‑cut steaks, fresh produce through Fresh Concepts, and artisanal cheeses via The Rind Cheese Company.

S&W serves a wide range of restaurant types, from donut shops and coffee shops to Tex‑Mex, Italian, Mediterranean, family dining, sandwich shops, and seafood establishments. Its customer base includes both independent operators and chain accounts, all supported by the company’s independent structure and partnerships with major suppliers like Unipro Foodservice, Campbell Foodservice, ConAgra Foodservice, Rich Products, Pillsbury, Hormel, General Mills, and Smithfield Foods.

The company’s guiding principle, coined by the founder, is "Large enough to serve, small enough to care." This philosophy drives its emphasis on personal relationships, quick reaction to customer needs without corporate red tape, and a commitment to helping operators grow their businesses. The combination of local ownership, disaster‑ready logistics, and curated product programs sets S&W apart in the regional foodservice market.

The company designs and manufactures low-voltage switchgear (UL 1558, UL 891), medium-voltage switchgear (5 kV–38 kV), DC switchgear, custom power distribution units (PDUs), and proprietary platforms such as Profusion™—an all-in-one PDU with sectionalized main disconnect, K-rated transformer, and integrated metering—and EVention™, a BABA-compliant power distribution platform for EV charging. Services span engineering design, system optimization, startup and commissioning, field measurement and retrofit, preventative maintenance, training, and power-quality monitoring. A new production center, three times the size of the previous facility, supports both custom and high-volume production.

SAI serves telecommunications, renewable energy integration, hydrogen generation, battery energy storage, and energy consulting sectors. Its market-focused business units target mission-critical facilities, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), commercial/industrial/government clients, emerging markets, and aftermarket support.

The company emphasizes “future-ready” innovation, citing patented products, a Teaming for Customer Success (TCS) program, and a supply-chain transformation that expanded manufacturing capacity.

about:
SPI Solar Panel Installation NC operates from Charlotte, North Carolina, as a locally owned and operated solar and roofing contractor serving homeowners across the state. The company was founded after its owners observed that out-of-state firms were making promises to North Carolina residents, sending subcontractors, and then disappearing once the job was done. While the exact founding year is not disclosed, the company reports over a decade of local experience.

The firm provides residential rooftop solar panel installation, solar panel repair, full roof installation, roof repair and replacement, roof inspection, home energy system monitoring, solar heat pump installation, home battery installation, Level 2 EV charger installation, home insulation and sealing, and solar shade installation. All work is performed by the company's own certified local team with no subcontractors. Installations are backed by a 25-year performance guarantee. The physical installation typically takes one to two days, while the full process from assessment to a live system runs four to eight weeks including permitting and utility approval.

The company serves residential homeowners throughout North Carolina, designing systems around each home's energy usage, roof condition, and budget. Its installations have collectively produced 25 million kilowatt-hours of clean solar energy, eliminating over 2,000 tons of CO2 annually — equivalent to 33,000 trees worth of carbon capture.

The business was started to offer a better alternative to the transient, subcontractor-driven model the founders encountered. It emphasizes local knowledge of North Carolina's climate, utility infrastructure, permit requirements, and available incentives, along with transparent pricing and dedicated aftercare support.

about:
Sag Harbor Industries, Inc. was founded in 1946 by Charles Edison, son of inventor Thomas Edison, in the village of Sag Harbor, New York. The company began with a single goal: to manufacture electrical coils and inductors of superior quality. Today it operates from two U.S. manufacturing locations — its original headquarters in Sag Harbor, NY, and a second facility in Farmville, North Carolina.

The company produces custom power, control, and instrumentation transformers and coils, along with cable assemblies, printed circuit board assemblies, and full box-build integration. Its coil portfolio spans electric, encapsulated, field, molded, self-supported, solenoid, varnished, and toroidal types, manufactured through winding, injection molding, transfer molding, and vacuum impregnation processes. The facilities are equipped with automated and semi-automated equipment geared for high-volume, medium-volume, and short-run production.

Sag Harbor serves electronics, aerospace, medical device, renewable energy, industrial automation, and automotive sectors. Aerospace customers receive UL-compliant components built to AS9100 standards; medical device makers rely on ISO 13485-certified, burr-free coils for implants and diagnostic equipment; renewable energy projects use toroidal coils and transformers for solar and wind systems; and automation firms source durable solenoid coils and cable assemblies for robotics and machinery.

The founder's original mandate — superior quality — remains the stated differentiator. The company emphasizes 100% U.S. manufacturing, engineering and design competence, flexible supply chain management, and on-time delivery. It holds ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, and ISO 13485 certifications, and its products meet UL insulation system standards.

about:
Savannah Food Company, based in Savannah, Tennessee, traces its roots to 1970 when Bob Hagy, after decades in the restaurant business, began producing hushpuppies using family recipes. The Catfish Hotel Restaurant, still operating today, had built a reputation for its freshly made hushpuppies, prompting Hagy to build a dedicated processing facility. In 2004, the company was acquired by John Bryan, whose family had founded Bryan Foods, Inc. in the early 1900s.

The company operates a food processing facility that manufactures hushpuppies and side dishes, including original, jalapeño, and sweet corn varieties. Its quality system incorporates a hazard analysis and critical control points (HACCP) plan, good manufacturing practices (GMP), and alignment with global food safety initiatives (GFSI). The facility has held FSSC 22000 certification since June 2013, a globally recognized food safety standard based on ISO principles.

Savannah Food Company supplies wholesome, easy-to-prepare hushpuppies and side dishes to customers seeking authentic Southern recipes. Its products are positioned as comparable to scratch-made family meals.

The business emphasizes food safety and quality as the responsibility of every employee, backed by preventive control management, continuous improvement, and the FSSC 22000 certification. The original processing facility was built to replicate the restaurant-quality hushpuppies that made the Catfish Hotel famous.

about:
Saw Logs to Lumber operates from a Boschertown building on North Highway 94 in St. Charles, Missouri. The company traces its start to 1994, when Wayne, a Vietnam War veteran and former Boeing technical representative, purchased the floodplain property after recognizing its highway visibility and proximity to his then-employer. Wayne’s woodworking roots reach back to age 13, when a neighbor’s unpaid debt led him to acquire a table saw and lumber, with which he built a boat and dock.

The shop runs two sawmills and maintains an inventory exceeding 50,000 board feet of live-edge slabs alongside more than 800 logs, all sourced from Missouri-native species such as walnut, cherry, oak, and sassafras. Beyond milling customer-supplied logs, the team produces custom furniture and accessories—tables, paddles, benches, charcuterie boards, bartops, and mantel pieces—while also selling dimensional lumber to contractors, builders, and DIY enthusiasts.

Customers range from professional contractors and builders seeking sustainable Missouri hardwood to hobbyists commissioning one-off pieces. The business also serves woodworkers who bring their own logs for custom milling, offering a full chain from raw log to finished slab or product.

Wayne describes himself as a “Tree Whisperer,” aiming to let each piece of wood “speak for itself” by revealing its unique grain and character. The venture began as a retirement pursuit after decades at Boeing, driven by a desire to honor the natural beauty of local timber rather than chase volume metrics.
